profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting between the systems and experimentation workstreams of an ML research project preparing an internal reproducibility package and a camera-ready artifact for a paper on scalable distributed training over public cloud GPU clusters. The project has a top-k sparsification communication library, a multi-level data caching mechanism, and a parallel tensor update operator already working on a 16-node Tencent Cloud setup, and the team now needs to align on what each side will hand off before the artifact freeze. The agenda is to confirm which benchmark runs will be treated as the official replication set, what the 'baseline' comparison bundle contains, how logs and configs will be packaged, and who updates the shared results sheet and artifact repository. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear division of labor: one member will prepare runnable training jobs and system configs, while the other will prepare the benchmark table and summary package for the paper appendix and internal review.

members.name: Lina Qiu
members.expertise: GPU cluster training systems, communication compression, experiment infrastructure, cloud deployment
members.background: Lina built most of the training runtime changes for the project, including the top-k communication library integration and the cache orchestration scripts for Tencent Cloud clusters, and she usually interfaces with infra-heavy artifact expectations.
members.private_state: She wants to minimize last-minute reruns on expensive cloud instances and protect the credibility of the systems numbers already obtained on the 16-node cluster; she is worried that any request framed vaguely will expand into additional packaging work or reruns she cannot staff this week.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'baseline bundle,' they mean the exact comparison runs already used in the latest internal draft: Horovod FP32 allreduce and the project system on the 16-node Tencent cluster, with logs and launch scripts tied to those runs.

A run is 'reproduced' once the training job completes end-to-end with matching throughput trends and final accuracy within normal run variance, not once every table-ready aggregation and appendix figure is regenerated.
The shared results sheet is owned by the experimentation side, while the systems side only uploads raw logs, configs, and launch commands into the artifact repository.
The 'cache-enabled config' naturally includes the local NVMe warm-cache stage because that is how all large ImageNet and Transformer runs were executed after the first week of tuning.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Benchmark design, empirical evaluation, large-scale vision and NLP training, paper artifact preparation
members.background: Arjun led the empirical study and wrote most of the paper sections comparing training speedups and final model quality across CNN and Transformer workloads, and he usually coordinates tables, appendix material, and reproducibility notes for submission.
members.private_state: He needs a clean, reviewer-friendly package that lets him finalize the comparison tables without reopening methodological debates, and he is concerned that raw systems outputs alone will not be enough to support the appendix and internal audit of claims.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'baseline bundle,' they mean the full comparison package behind the paper tables, including the tuned dense baseline, the sparsified system, and the ablation variants used to justify caching and the parallel tensor operator.
A run is 'reproduced' only when the final summary artifacts are regenerated in the same form as the paper claims: cleaned CSVs, averaged numbers, and table-ready outputs for each benchmark family.
The person who generated the runs is also responsible for updating the shared results sheet with canonical numbers, because otherwise provenance gets lost.

The 'cache-enabled config' refers to turning on the multi-level caching feature in the codepath, while whether the cache is prewarmed or cold-started is part of normal execution and does not need separate mention.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the baseline bundle
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to package the 'baseline bundle' for the artifact freeze.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks this means only the core head-to-head runs already highlighted in the latest draft: the production dense baseline and the final system runs on the official 16-node setup.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks this includes the broader comparison package underlying the paper tables: core baseline, final system, and supporting ablations for caching and the parallel tensor operator.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have repeatedly used 'baseline bundle' in project chat as shorthand for 'the comparison material,' and because they are coordinating packaging rather than debating experiment design, neither expects the scope itself to need explicit restatement.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that certain runs just need to be 'reproduced' before internal review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes reproduction means rerunning jobs successfully and verifying that throughput and final accuracy are consistent with prior logs within ordinary noise.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes reproduction means regenerating the polished downstream summaries used in the paper, including averaged result files and appendix-ready tables.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML research meetings, 'reproduced' often flexibly refers to either rerunning experiments or recreating reported outputs; because both outcomes usually travel together, the criterion gap remains hidden during a brief coordination discussion.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use the 'cache-enabled config' for the ImageNet and Transformer replication jobs.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means using the operational recipe from prior cluster runs, including a prewarmed local NVMe cache stage before the timed training job starts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means enabling the multi-level caching option in the training config, with runs starting from a normal cold state unless prewarming is called out separately.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are focused on coordination and both view their interpretation as the obvious default implementation detail of the same feature, so the phrase sounds fully resolved while hiding a meaningful procedural difference.

misalignment_points.topic: Ownership of the shared results sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the numbers will be 'in the shared sheet' before the appendix draft is circulated.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes M2 or the experimentation side will ingest raw logs and update the canonical sheet, since that sheet is part of paper-facing analysis.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes M1 will populate the sheet with the canonical numbers because she owns the run provenance and generated the jobs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Ownership has evolved informally across prior deadlines and neither person experiences their assumption as a decision point; the phrase 'in the shared sheet' sounds like a status checkpoint rather than an assignment.
